nodes.name: Product catalog domain
nodes.summary: Django models, query sets, search indexing and Celery tasks for products, variants, categories, collections and media.
nodes.detail: The saleor/product package holds the catalog data model and the domain logic around it. Products belong to a product type and an optional category tree; each product has variants that carry the stock keeping unit (SKU). Visibility and price are per channel: a ProductChannelListing says whether a product is published and visible in a channel, and a ProductVariantChannelListing holds the variant price, cost price, prior price and the precomputed discounted price. Query sets in managers.py decide what a shopper or staff member may see. Background Celery tasks rebuild the product search vector, fetch remote media images, rename variants and recalculate discounted prices when promotions change.

nodes.name: Promotion price pipeline
nodes.summary: Two-stage dirty-flag pipeline that turns catalogue promotions into stored discounted prices on product and variant channel listings.
nodes.detail: Catalogue promotions are not applied when a price is read; they are precomputed. Stage one: any change that can affect which variants a promotion rule covers sets PromotionRule.variants_dirty. A Celery beat task re-evaluates the rule's catalogue predicate, rewrites the rule-to-variant relation and marks affected ProductChannelListing rows with discounted_price_dirty. Stage two: another beat task picks up to 2,000 dirty listings, computes the best promotion discount per variant and channel, stores discounted_price_amount on variant and product listings, records which rule produced it, and emits product variant discounted price webhooks. Both tasks re-queue themselves until no dirty rows remain.
facts: Both beat entries run every BEAT_PRICE_RECALCULATION_SCHEDULE, default 30 seconds (saleor/saleor/settings.py:662)
Rule batch: 50 rules per run (PROMOTION_RULE_BATCH_SIZE in product/tasks.py)
Listing batch: 2,000 product channel listings per run (DISCOUNTED_PRODUCT_BATCH)

nodes.name: Product GraphQL API
nodes.summary: Graphene types, queries, filters, data loaders and mutations that expose products, variants, categories, collections and product types.
nodes.detail: The saleor/graphql/product package registers ProductQueries and ProductMutations in the root schema (saleor/graphql/api.py). Queries resolve through channel-aware query sets and return ChannelContext wrappers so nested fields know which channel's listing, pricing and availability to show. Filtering supports the deprecated filter input and the newer where input, plus full-text search over the product search vector. Mutations validate input, save through Django models, mark search vectors and promotion rules dirty, and call plugin manager events that become webhooks.

nodes.name: Product mutations
nodes.summary: Single-object mutations for products, variants, media, categories, collections, product types and channel listings.
nodes.detail: Each mutation is a Graphene class with clean_input, save and post-save steps. Product and variant saves set search_index_dirty so the search beat task reindexes them. Changes that can move a product in or out of a promotion (category, collections, variants, channel listings) call mark_active_catalogue_promotion_rules_as_dirty or mark_products_in_channels_as_dirty, which feed the promotion price pipeline. Events such as product_created and product_updated go through the plugin manager, which fans them out to webhooks.

nodes.name: Bulk product mutations
nodes.summary: Batch create, update and delete mutations for products, variants, stocks, media, categories, collections and product types.
nodes.detail: Bulk mutations validate every row first and collect errors per input index. An error policy decides what happens on failure: reject everything (default), reject only failed rows, or ignore failed rows. Valid rows are written with bulk_create inside one transaction, then webhooks are sent per created object and promotion rules for the touched channels are marked dirty.

nodes.name: Attributes
nodes.summary: Typed attributes and their values, assigned to product types, variant selection, page types and customer types, and their GraphQL API.
nodes.detail: An Attribute has an input type (dropdown, multiselect, file, reference, numeric, rich text, plain text, swatch, boolean, date, date-time) and a type (product type, page type or customer type). Attributes are attached to product types through AttributeProduct (product level) and AttributeVariant (variant level, optionally used for variant selection), and to page types through AttributePage. Concrete values live in AttributeValue rows and are linked to products, variants, pages and users by assignment tables. The GraphQL layer validates attribute input per input type with type handlers and saves it through AttributeAssignmentMixin.

nodes.name: Pages and menus
nodes.summary: Content models (pages with page types and attributes) and navigation menus, with their GraphQL queries and mutations.
nodes.detail: Pages are publishable content entries whose structure comes from a PageType and its attributes, so they double as a lightweight content model (for example size guides or brand pages). They have their own search vector, rebuilt by a beat task. Menus are trees of MenuItem rows (Modified Preorder Tree Traversal, MPTT) that link to a category, collection, page or plain URL; the AssignNavigation mutation sets the site's main and secondary menu.

nodes.name: Channels
nodes.summary: Sales channels: the unit that scopes currency, country, warehouses, shipping zones, listings, promotions and order and checkout settings.
nodes.detail: A Channel row has a slug, a currency code, a default country and an active flag. Nearly every commercial record is keyed by channel: product, variant and collection channel listings, voucher channel listings, promotion rules, shipping method listings and tax configuration. Warehouses and shipping zones join channels through many-to-many relations defined on their own models. The channel also stores operational settings: stock allocation strategy, mark-as-paid strategy, default transaction flow, order expiry, checkout automatic completion and the draft order price freeze period.

nodes.name: Promotions and vouchers
nodes.summary: Discount domain: promotions with catalogue or order rules, vouchers with codes, and the discount rows applied to checkouts and orders.
nodes.detail: Promotions replace the older sales. A Promotion has a type (catalogue or order), start and end dates and rules. A catalogue rule holds a catalogue predicate (products, variants, categories, collections combined with AND and OR), a reward value and type (fixed or percentage) and the channels it applies to; its matching variants are cached in PromotionRule_Variants. An order rule holds an order predicate and gives a subtotal discount or a gift. Vouchers are codes with per-channel values, minimum spend, usage limits and once-per-customer rules. Applied discounts are stored as CheckoutDiscount, CheckoutLineDiscount, OrderDiscount and OrderLineDiscount rows created by the utilities here and called from checkout and order code.

nodes.name: Discount GraphQL API
nodes.summary: Queries and mutations for promotions, promotion rules, vouchers, voucher codes and the deprecated sale API.
nodes.detail: DiscountQueries exposes promotions, vouchers and the deprecated sales; DiscountMutations covers promotion and rule create, update and delete, voucher management and the sale mutations kept for backward compatibility. Promotion mutations decide whether a rule needs its variants recomputed and either set variants_dirty or mark the affected products dirty directly, so the price pipeline recalculates discounted prices in the background. Catalogue predicates are turned into variant query sets by graphql/discount/utils.py, which the domain tasks also import.

nodes.name: Thumbnails and media
nodes.summary: On-demand thumbnail generation and original image redirects for product media, categories, collections, users and app logos.
nodes.detail: Image fields store originals in Django's default storage. GraphQL types return a proxy address (/thumbnail/<id>/<size>/<format>/) when no thumbnail exists yet. The unauthenticated view behind that address resolves the global ID, rounds the size up to an allowed size, returns a redirect if a Thumbnail row already exists, and otherwise decodes the original with Pillow, resizes it, saves the new file to storage, records a Thumbnail row and emits a thumbnail_created event. Remote product media are downloaded by a Celery task first; until then the views answer 503 with Retry-After.

nodes.name: CSV product export
nodes.summary: Asynchronous export of products to comma-separated values (CSV) or Excel files stored in object storage, with notifications and cleanup.
nodes.detail: The exportProducts mutation creates an ExportFile job row and an export started event, then queues a Celery task. The task filters products by ids or by the product filter, writes headers and rows in batches of 1,000 products into a temporary file with petl, saves it to Django's default storage (object storage in typical deployments), marks the job successful and notifies plugins with a download link. Failures set the job to failed and send a failure notification. A nightly beat task deletes files older than EXPORT_FILES_TIMEDELTA.
facts: Cleanup beat entry runs daily at 01:00 (delete-old-export-files)

nodes.name: Catalog data model
nodes.summary: Django models for categories, product types, products, variants, channel listings, media, collections and their translations.
nodes.detail: Category is an MPTT (Modified Preorder Tree Traversal) tree with search indexes on name, slug and plain-text description. Product points to a ProductType (kind normal or gift card, shipping flag, weight, tax class) and optionally to a Category; it keeps a search_document, a search_vector and a search_index_dirty flag. ProductVariant carries the SKU (stock keeping unit), inventory tracking and per-customer quantity limit. Per-channel data lives in ProductChannelListing (published flag and date, visible in listings, available for purchase date, discounted price) and ProductVariantChannelListing (price, cost price, prior price, discounted price, availability flag, linked promotion rules). Collections join products through CollectionProduct and have their own channel listings. Translations exist for categories, products, variants, media and collections.

nodes.name: Category
nodes.summary: Category tree node with slug, rich-text description, background image and search index.
nodes.detail: Uses django-mptt so descendants can be fetched in one query; the parent foreign key cascades on delete, so deleting a category deletes its subtree. Products keep their row but lose the category (SET_NULL).

nodes.name: ProductType
nodes.summary: Template for products: kind (normal or gift card), shipping requirement, default weight and tax class.
nodes.detail: Attributes are attached to product types through AttributeProduct and AttributeVariant. The has_variants flag is deprecated and no longer affects variant creation.

nodes.name: Product
nodes.summary: A sellable item: type, category, rich description, search vector, default variant, rating and tax class.
nodes.detail: Search uses three GIN (generalized inverted) indexes: trigram on search_document, full text on search_vector and trigram on name and slug. search_index_dirty marks rows for the search beat task. The default_variant is set to the first variant created.
facts: Product.objects is ProductManager built from ProductsQueryset

nodes.name: ProductChannelListing
nodes.summary: Per-channel publication of a product: published flag and date, visible in listings, purchase date and cached discounted price.
nodes.detail: Inherits is_published and published_at from PublishableModel. discounted_price_amount holds the cheapest discounted variant price in the channel, written by the price pipeline; discounted_price_dirty queues the row for recalculation. Unique per product and channel.

nodes.name: ProductVariant
nodes.summary: A purchasable variant of a product with SKU, weight, inventory tracking and per-customer quantity limit.
nodes.detail: SKU means stock keeping unit. Variant attributes define the variant; preorder fields remain only until removal after version 3.24. Weight falls back to product then product type weight.

nodes.name: ProductVariant.get_price()
nodes.summary: Returns the stored discounted price, or applies promotion rules to an overridden price.
nodes.detail: Without a price override the method trusts the precomputed discounted_price on the listing, falling back to the base price. With an override (for example a custom line price) it recomputes the discount from the given promotion rules.
nodes.signature: def get_price(self, channel_listing: "ProductVariantChannelListing", price_override: Optional["Decimal"] = None, promotion_rules: Iterable["PromotionRule"] | None = None) -> "Money"

nodes.name: ProductVariantChannelListing
nodes.summary: Per-channel variant price, cost price, prior price, discounted price, availability flag and applied promotion rules.
nodes.detail: A listing is sellable when price_amount is set and is_available_for_purchase is true (the is_sellable property, twin of managers.sellable_listing_q). promotion_rules is a many-to-many through VariantChannelListingPromotionRule.

nodes.name: VariantChannelListingPromotionRule
nodes.summary: Join row recording which promotion rule produced a variant listing's discount and the discount amount.
nodes.detail: Written by the price pipeline and read by checkout and order code (fetch_variant_rules_info) to build line discounts with the promotion name.

nodes.name: ProductMedia
nodes.summary: Image or external video attached to a product, with alt text, external URL and oEmbed data.
nodes.detail: When created from an external image address the image field is empty until fetch_product_media_image_task downloads it.

nodes.name: Collection
nodes.summary: Hand-curated group of products with slug, description and background image.
nodes.detail: Products join through the sortable CollectionProduct model; publication per channel lives in CollectionChannelListing.

nodes.name: Catalog visibility query sets
nodes.summary: Query sets that decide which products, variants and collections a requestor can see in a channel.
nodes.detail: ProductsQueryset.published keeps products with a published listing in an active channel whose publication date has passed. published_with_variants additionally requires at least one sellable variant listing (price set and available for purchase). visible_to_user grants staff and apps with manage products, manage orders or manage discounts permission every product, or only those listed in the given channel when the query is channel-limited; everyone else sees published products with sellable variants. Variant and collection query sets follow the same pattern.

nodes.name: ProductsQueryset.visible_to_user()
nodes.summary: Chooses the product set a user or app may see based on permissions, channel and whether access is channel-limited.
nodes.signature: def visible_to_user(self, requestor: Union["User", "App", None], channel: Channel | None, limited_channel_access: bool)

nodes.name: ProductsQueryset.published_with_variants()
nodes.summary: Published products in an active channel that have at least one sellable variant listing.

nodes.name: Product search indexer
nodes.summary: Builds the PostgreSQL full-text search vector for products from name, description, attributes and variants.
nodes.detail: update_products_search_vector reads products from the replica in batches of 100, resolves page titles for page-reference attribute values, and computes a weighted vector: product name (weight A), plain-text description (weight C), attribute values and variant names and SKUs (stock keeping units). It bulk-updates search_vector and clears search_index_dirty. The GraphQL products query matches against this vector with core.search.prefix_search.
facts: Inner batch size: 100 products (PRODUCTS_BATCH_SIZE in product/search.py)

nodes.name: update_products_search_vector()
nodes.summary: Recomputes and saves search vectors for the given product ids in replica-read batches.

nodes.name: prepare_product_search_vector_value()
nodes.summary: Returns the weighted list of search vectors for one product.
nodes.signature: def prepare_product_search_vector_value(product: "Product", *, already_prefetched=False, page_id_to_title_map: dict[int, str] | None = None) -> list[NoValidationSearchVector]

nodes.name: Catalog Celery tasks
nodes.summary: Celery tasks for promotion rule variants, discounted price recalculation, search reindexing, media download and variant naming.
nodes.detail: Two beat-driven tasks implement the promotion price pipeline and re-queue themselves until done. update_products_search_vector_task reindexes up to 300 dirty products per run on the search queue. fetch_product_media_image_task downloads an external image with retries and validates status, content type, MIME (media type) and pixel count before saving. collection_product_updated_task sends product_updated webhooks after collection changes. update_variants_names regenerates names when variant selection attributes change. deactivate_preorder_for_variants_task runs hourly for leftover preorder variants.
facts: fetch_product_media_image_task: max 5 retries with backoff on IOError

nodes.name: Rule-variant refresh task (stage one)
nodes.summary: Stage one of the price pipeline: recomputes variants for dirty catalogue rules and marks affected product listings dirty.
nodes.detail: Selects up to 50 rules of active catalogue promotions with variants_dirty set and a non-empty reward and predicate. It captures the rule's current variants, recomputes them from the predicate, builds a channel-to-products map from old and new variants, clears variants_dirty under a row lock, marks the product listings dirty and re-queues itself.
nodes.code:
with transaction.atomic():
            promotion_rule_ids = list(
                PromotionRule.objects.select_for_update(of=("self",))
                .filter(pk__in=ids, variants_dirty=True)
                .order_by("pk")
                .values_list("id", flat=True)
            )
            PromotionRule.objects.filter(pk__in=promotion_rule_ids).update(
                variants_dirty=False
            )

        mark_products_in_channels_as_dirty(channel_to_product_map, allow_replica=True)
        update_variant_relations_for_active_promotion_rules_task.delay()

nodes.name: Discounted price recalculation task (stage two)
nodes.summary: Stage two of the price pipeline: recalculates discounted prices for up to 2,000 dirty product listings and re-queues itself.
nodes.detail: Reads dirty listings from the replica, recalculates prices only for those listings, sends discounted price webhooks for changed variants, then clears discounted_price_dirty under select_for_update before queueing the next batch.
nodes.code:
changed_prices = update_discounted_prices_for_promotion(
            products, only_dirty_products=True
        )
        _send_variant_price_updated_webhooks(changed_prices)
        with transaction.atomic():
            channel_listings_ids = list(
                ProductChannelListing.objects.select_for_update(of=("self",))
                .filter(id__in=listing_ids, discounted_price_dirty=True)
                .order_by("pk")
                .values_list("id", flat=True)
            )
            ProductChannelListing.objects.filter(id__in=channel_listings_ids).update(
                discounted_price_dirty=False
            )
        recalculate_discounted_price_for_products_task.delay()

nodes.name: _send_variant_price_updated_webhooks()
nodes.summary: Emits PRODUCT_VARIANT_DISCOUNTED_PRICE_UPDATED through the plugin manager for every changed variant price.

nodes.name: update_products_search_vector_task()
nodes.summary: Beat task on the search queue that reindexes up to 300 products flagged search_index_dirty, oldest update first.

nodes.name: fetch_product_media_image_task()
nodes.summary: Downloads an external product image, validates it and stores it; on final failure deletes the media row.
nodes.detail: Uses HTTPClient with streaming and no redirects. Rejects bad status codes, mismatched content types, unsupported MIME (media) types and images over the pixel limit (ImageTooLargeError). Permanent validation errors are not retried; IOError is retried with backoff.

nodes.name: collection_product_updated_task()
nodes.summary: Sends product_updated webhooks for products whose collection membership changed, reading from replica with a writer fallback.

nodes.name: deactivate_preorder_for_variants_task()
nodes.summary: Hourly task that ends preorder on variants whose preorder end date has passed.

nodes.name: Storefront pricing and availability
nodes.summary: Computes price ranges, undiscounted and prior prices, discounts and on-sale flags for products and variants with taxes applied.
nodes.detail: get_product_availability takes the product listing and its variant listings and builds TaxedMoneyRange values for price, discounted_price and prior_price, applying the channel's tax rate and whether prices are entered with tax. A product is on sale when it is visible and has a discount. get_variant_availability does the same for one variant. Called from the GraphQL pricing resolvers.

nodes.name: get_product_availability()
nodes.summary: Builds the product pricing block: discounted, undiscounted and prior price ranges, discount amounts and on-sale flag.
nodes.signature: def get_product_availability(*, product_channel_listing: ProductChannelListing | None, variants_channel_listing: list[ProductVariantChannelListing], prices_entered_with_tax: bool, tax_calculation_strategy: str, tax_rate: Decimal) -> ProductAvailability

nodes.name: fetch_variants_for_promotion_rules()
nodes.summary: Evaluates each rule's catalogue predicate against the replica and rewrites the rule-to-variant relation.

nodes.name: delete_categories()
nodes.summary: Deletes categories with their subtrees, unpublishes their products and sends webhooks.
nodes.detail: The channel ids passed to mark_active_catalogue_promotion_rules_as_dirty are read from a lazy query set that filters listings by products of the deleted categories. It is evaluated after the delete, when those products no longer reference the category, so the set is likely empty (see findings).

nodes.name: Recalculate all discounted prices command
nodes.summary: Management command that recalculates discounted prices for every product in batches of 500.
nodes.detail: Iterates all products by primary key and calls update_discounted_prices_for_promotion for each batch. Unlike the beat task, it discards the returned price changes, so no discounted price webhooks are sent, and it does not clear discounted_price_dirty flags.

nodes.name: Discounted price calculator
nodes.summary: Computes and stores discounted prices on product and variant channel listings from active catalogue promotion rules.
nodes.detail: update_discounted_prices_for_promotion loads, from the replica, the variants of the given products, the map of variant to applicable promotion rules, the variant listings per product and channel and the existing listing-to-rule rows. For each product channel listing it computes each variant's best discount, clamps prices at zero, and sets the product listing's discounted price to the cheapest variant. Changed rows are bulk-updated, listing-to-rule rows created or updated, stale ones deleted, and a list of price changes is returned for webhooks.

nodes.name: update_discounted_prices_for_promotion()
nodes.summary: Recalculates discounted prices for the given products, optionally only for listings flagged dirty, and returns the changes.
nodes.signature: def update_discounted_prices_for_promotion(products: ProductsQueryset, only_dirty_products: bool = False ) -> list[VariantDiscountedPriceChange]

nodes.name: _get_discounted_variants_prices_for_promotions()
nodes.summary: Per variant listing: picks the best rule discount, clamps at zero, records the rule and collects price changes.
nodes.signature: def _get_discounted_variants_prices_for_promotions(variant_listings: list[ProductVariantChannelListing], rules_info_per_variant: dict[int, list[PromotionRuleInfo]], channel: Channel, variant_listing_to_listing_rule_per_rule_map: dict) -> tuple[ list[Money], list[ProductVariantChannelListing], list[V

for variant_listing in variant_listings:
        applied_discount = calculate_discounted_price_for_promotions(
            price=variant_listing.price,
            rules_info_per_variant=rules_info_per_variant,
            channel=channel,
            variant_id=variant_listing.variant_id,

nodes.name: Dirty-flag markers
nodes.summary: Marks product channel listings as needing discounted price recalculation, from rules or from a channel-to-products map.
nodes.detail: mark_products_in_channels_as_dirty finds listings for the given channel and product pairs, locks the ones not yet dirty in primary key order (to avoid deadlocks) and sets discounted_price_dirty. get_channel_to_products_map_from_rules derives that map from a rule's variants and channels.

nodes.name: mark_products_in_channels_as_dirty()
nodes.summary: Sets discounted_price_dirty on product listings for the given channel and product pairs under row locks.

nodes.summary: Marks product listings dirty for every product and channel covered by the given promotion rules.

nodes.name: Product schema root
nodes.summary: Declares ProductQueries (products, variants, categories, collections, product types, sales report) and ProductMutations.
nodes.detail: Each query field declares its filter, where, sort and search arguments and a channel slug. Resolvers default the channel for requestors without catalog permissions, load the channel by slug through a data loader and pass a channel-scoped query set to the connection builder. ProductMutations maps every product, variant, media, category, collection, product type and channel listing mutation to a field.

nodes.name: ProductQueries.resolve_products()
nodes.summary: Resolver for the products query: permission check, default channel, search, filters and pagination.
nodes.detail: Requestors without manage products, orders or discounts permission must have a channel; if none is given the single default channel is used or an error is raised. Search applies prefix_search over the search vector and enables ranking.

nodes.name: ProductMutations
nodes.summary: Graphene object type mapping catalog mutation names to mutation classes.

nodes.name: resolve_products()
nodes.summary: Applies visible_to_user and, for customers, keeps only products visible in listings in the channel.
nodes.signature: def resolve_products(info: ResolveInfo, requestor, channel: Channel | None, limited_channel_access: bool) -> ChannelQsContext

nodes.name: Product filters
nodes.summary: django-filter filter sets and where inputs for products, variants, categories, collections and product types.
nodes.detail: ProductFilter backs the deprecated filter argument and ProductWhere the where argument. Helpers filter by price range in a channel, minimal discounted price, category subtree, collections, stock availability per channel, warehouse quantities, publication and availability dates and attribute values (with range, date and boolean variants).

nodes.name: Product filter sets
nodes.summary: ProductFilter and ProductWhere: channel-aware filter sets used by the products query and by the CSV export.
nodes.detail: ProductFilter (filter argument, deprecated) and ProductWhere (where argument) are django-filter filter sets. Channel-dependent filters (price, minimal price, publication, availability, stock) resolve the channel from the input first. Attribute filters accept slugs with values, numeric and date ranges and booleans. export_products reuses ProductFilter so an export matches what the dashboard list shows.

nodes.name: ProductFilter
nodes.summary: Deprecated filter-style product filter set; also reused by export_products.

nodes.name: Product GraphQL types
nodes.summary: Graphene types for Product, ProductVariant, ProductType, ProductMedia, categories, collections and channel listings.
nodes.detail: Types are channel-aware: a ChannelContext carries the channel slug, and resolvers load listings, pricing and thumbnails through data loaders. Pricing resolvers combine listings with tax configuration, tax class rates and the shopper's country to produce taxed price ranges.

nodes.name: Product and variant types
nodes.summary: Product, ProductVariant, ProductType and ProductMedia Graphene types with pricing, availability, thumbnail and attribute fields.
nodes.detail: Product and ProductVariant extend ChannelContextType, so every field knows the channel slug from the parent query. Pricing resolvers chain data loaders for the channel, the product and variant listings, the tax class and tax configuration, then call the availability helpers. Thumbnail resolvers return a stored thumbnail URL or the proxy URL that creates one on first request. Attribute fields load assigned attributes with storefront visibility applied for customers.

nodes.name: Product.resolve_pricing()
nodes.summary: Loads channel, listings and tax data, then returns ProductPricingInfo with taxed price ranges for the channel.

nodes.name: Product.resolve_thumbnail()
nodes.summary: Returns a stored thumbnail URL or a thumbnail proxy URL for the product's first image.
nodes.signature: def resolve_thumbnail(root: ChannelContext[models.Product], info, *, size: int = 256, size_rounding: ThumbnailSizeRounding | None = None, format: str | None = None)

nodes.name: Product data loaders
nodes.summary: Batching data loaders for products, variants, listings, media, collections, categories and thumbnails.
nodes.detail: Data loaders group per-request lookups by key (for example product id and channel slug) to avoid one query per field. They read from the replica when the request allows it.

nodes.name: ProductCreate
nodes.summary: productCreate: validates input and attributes, saves the product with search_index_dirty set and fires product_created.
nodes.detail: save runs in a transaction: the product is saved with search_index_dirty true and attributes are written with AttributeAssignmentMixin.save. Collections are set in _save_m2m. post_save_action reloads the product and calls the plugin manager's product_created event. The product is not yet in any channel.

nodes.name: ProductUpdate
nodes.summary: productUpdate: saves changes, marks search dirty, marks promotion rules dirty in the product's channels and fires product_updated.
nodes.detail: Because category or collection changes can move the product into or out of a promotion predicate, every update marks active catalogue rules for the product's channels as variants_dirty.

nodes.name: ProductDelete
nodes.summary: productDelete: removes variants and draft order lines, queues order recalculation and fires product_deleted.

nodes.name: ProductMediaCreate
nodes.summary: productMediaCreate: stores an upload or schedules fetch_product_media_image_task for an external image.

nodes.name: Other product mutations
nodes.summary: Media update, delete and reorder mutations and the shared product input cleaner.
nodes.detail: Media update, delete and reorder keep media sort order; product_cleaner validates weight, slug and the rich-text description shared by create and update.

nodes.name: ProductVariantCreate
nodes.summary: productVariantCreate: saves the variant, sets it as default if first, creates stocks and attributes, names it, marks search and rules dirty.
nodes.detail: After save the product's search_index_dirty is set and product_variant_created fires; post_save_action marks active catalogue rules in the product's channels dirty so a matching promotion is applied once the variant gets a price.

nodes.name: ProductVariantUpdate
nodes.summary: productVariantUpdate: saves changes, reindexes the product and marks promotion rules dirty in its channels.

nodes.name: Other variant mutations
nodes.summary: Variant delete, reorder, set default, media assign and unassign, and the variant input cleaner.
nodes.detail: ProductVariantDelete also removes draft order lines for the variant, queues order recalculation and marks promotion rules dirty.

nodes.name: Channel listing mutations

ProductVariantChannelListingUpdate sets price, cost price and prior price per channel and copies price into discounted price until the price pipeline recalculates. Both mark the touched product and channel pairs dirty.

nodes.summary: productTypeCreate, productTypeUpdate and productTypeDelete.

nodes.name: productBulkCreate mutation
nodes.summary: Creates many products with attributes, media, channel listings and variants in one transaction.

nodes.name: ProductBulkCreate

nodes.detail: perform_mutation runs in a single transaction. Rows are cleaned with errors collected per index; with the default reject-everything policy any error returns all errors and writes nothing. Products, media and channel listings are bulk_created, attributes saved, variants created through the variant bulk logic, and media image downloads scheduled on commit. post_save_actions sends product_created and product_variant_created webhooks and marks rules dirty for the touched channels.

nodes.name: Attribute data model
nodes.summary: Attribute, AttributeValue, translations and the assignment tables linking them to product types, products, variants, pages and users.

nodes.name: Attribute and value models
nodes.summary: Attribute and AttributeValue models, their query sets and the bulk get-or-create value manager.
nodes.detail: Attribute carries input_type, type (product, page or customer type), entity_type for reference attributes, value_required and visible_in_storefront flags, unit and many-to-many links to the types that use it. AttributeValue stores the value in a column that matches the input type and may reference a product, variant, category, collection or page. AttributeValueManager adds bulk get-or-create and update-or-create used by the GraphQL save path.

nodes.name: Attribute

nodes.name: AttributeValue

Product and page indexers both call it.

nodes.name: Channel
nodes.summary: A sales channel: slug, currency code, default country, active flag and many operational settings.

ChannelUpdate tracks changed fields, adds or removes shipping zones (deleting shipping method listings for removed zones) and warehouses, and adjusts voucher usage when the draft-order voucher flag flips. ChannelDelete can move orders to a target channel and deletes checkouts.

nodes.name: BaseChannelListingMutation

Warehouses and countries are resolved through data loaders; some fields, such as name, are permission fields that require an authenticated app or staff user.

nodes.name: Discount data model
nodes.summary: Promotion, PromotionRule, Voucher, VoucherCode, voucher listings and the checkout and order discount rows.
nodes.detail: Promotion has a type, dates and last_notification_scheduled_at used by the toggle task. PromotionRule stores channels, catalogue and order predicates as JSON (JavaScript Object Notation), reward value, value type and reward type, gift variants, a cached variants relation and the variants_dirty flag. Voucher holds type, usage limit, dates, apply once per order or customer, single use, staff only and catalogue restrictions; VoucherCode rows hold the codes and their usage counters; VoucherChannelListing holds per-channel value and minimum spend. BaseDiscount and its subclasses store applied discounts on checkouts, checkout lines, orders and order lines.

nodes.name: Promotion
nodes.summary: Catalogue or order promotion with name, description, start and end dates and rules.

nodes.name: PromotionRule
nodes.summary: Rule of a promotion: channels, catalogue or order predicate, reward, gifts, cached variants and variants_dirty flag.

nodes.name: PromotionRule.get_discount()
nodes.summary: Returns a partial function applying the rule's fixed or percentage reward in a currency.

nodes.name: Voucher
nodes.summary: Discount code definition: type, limits, dates, per-customer and staff-only rules and catalogue restrictions.

nodes.name: VoucherCode
nodes.summary: A redeemable code of a voucher with usage count and active flag.

nodes.name: VoucherChannelListing
nodes.summary: Per-channel voucher value, currency and minimum spend.

nodes.name: BaseDiscount
nodes.summary: Abstract applied-discount row: type, value type, value, amount, reason, promotion rule, voucher and code.

nodes.name: Promotion engine
nodes.summary: Promotion discount math, rule-to-variant maintenance, dirty marking, and order-promotion and gift handling for checkouts and orders.
nodes.detail: Catalogue side: calculate_discounted_price_for_promotions picks the best applicable rule per variant and channel, get_variants_to_promotion_rules_map builds the variant-to-rules map for active promotions, update_rule_variant_relation rewrites PromotionRule_Variants under ordered row locks, and the mark_* helpers set variants_dirty. Order side: get_best_rule compares subtotal discounts and gift rewards; create_discount_objects_for_order_promotions creates or removes order-level discounts and gift lines on a checkout or order.

nodes.summary: Evaluates every rule valid in the channel and keeps the one with the largest discount amount.

nodes.summary: Maps variant ids to rules of active promotions, with each rule's channel ids, reading the replica.

nodes.name: update_rule_variant_relation()
nodes.summary: Diffs old and new rule-to-variant pairs and applies deletes and inserts under ordered row locks to avoid deadlocks.

nodes.name: mark_active_catalogue_rules_as_dirty()
nodes.summary: Sets variants_dirty on active catalogue rules in the given channels so the price pipeline re-evaluates them.
nodes.code:
with transaction.atomic():
        rule_ids_to_update = list(
            PromotionRule.objects.select_for_update(of=("self",))
            .filter(id__in=rule_ids, variants_dirty=False)
            .order_by("pk")
            .values_list("id", flat=True)
        )
        PromotionRule.objects.filter(id__in=rule_ids_to_update).update(
            variants_dirty=True
        )

nodes.summary: Sets variants_dirty on all rules of the given promotions.

nodes.name: Voucher engine

nodes.detail: validate_voucher checks minimum spend, minimum quantity, once per customer and staff only. increase_voucher_usage bumps code usage when there is a limit, records customer usage when once-per-customer applies and deactivates single-use codes. Line-level and order-level voucher discounts are computed and stored for orders, including vouchers that apply once per order to the cheapest line.

nodes.summary: Runs the voucher's minimum spend, quantity, once-per-customer and staff-only checks.

nodes.name: Checkout discount builder
nodes.summary: Creates checkout line discounts for catalogue promotions and checkout discounts for order promotions.

Order promotions are evaluated against the checkout subtotal and stored as one CheckoutDiscount or a gift line. Base prices on lines are then refreshed and the soonest promotion end date is returned so prices expire in time.

nodes.name: Order discount builder
nodes.summary: Creates and refreshes order line discounts for catalogue promotions, order promotions and manual discounts.
nodes.detail: Mirrors the checkout builder for orders: catalogue promotion line discounts are prepared from variant listing rules and written with create_order_line_discount_objects, order promotions create OrderDiscount rows or gift lines, and manual line discounts are refreshed. Base unit prices on order lines are recalculated after discounts change.

Voucher helpers release or recount code usage of draft orders when a channel setting changes.

nodes.name: Thumbnail and image views
nodes.summary: Unauthenticated Django views that create or redirect to thumbnails and original images.
nodes.detail: Two plain Django views, not GraphQL. handle_thumbnail maps the global ID type to a model and image field, checks format and size, serves an existing thumbnail by redirect and otherwise creates and stores one before redirecting. handle_original_image redirects to the stored original. Both read from the replica and answer 503 with Retry-After 60 while a remote product image is still pending.

nodes.name: handle_thumbnail()
nodes.summary: Resolves the instance, returns an existing thumbnail or creates one with Pillow, saves it to storage and redirects.
nodes.detail: Supported types: User, Category, Collection, ProductMedia, App and AppInstallation. Formats are limited to the allowed set (AVIF and WEBP, WEBP only for icons); sizes round up to the allowed list. Oversized images return 400 and are logged at warning level because the view is unauthenticated.
nodes.signature: def handle_thumbnail(request, instance_id: str, size: str, format: str | None = None)

nodes.name: handle_original_image()
nodes.summary: Redirects to the stored original image, or answers 503 while a remote product image is still being fetched.

nodes.name: Thumbnail processing
nodes.summary: Thumbnail URL helpers, size rounding and the Pillow-based ProcessedImage pipeline.
nodes.detail: prepare_image_proxy_url reverses the thumbnail route with a global id; get_thumbnail_size rounds to the allowed sizes (up by default). ProcessedImage opens the source from storage, detects the MIME (media) type with libmagic, rejects decompression bombs, applies EXIF (exchangeable image file format) orientation and format-specific preprocessing and saves at quality 70.

nodes.name: ProcessedImage
nodes.summary: Opens, validates, resizes and encodes an image into a thumbnail file.
facts: Progressive JPEG and lossless WEBP are off

nodes.name: get_image_or_proxy_url()
nodes.summary: Returns the stored thumbnail URL, or the proxy URL that generates it on first request.

flows.name: A product is created and published to a channel
flows.summary: Staff create a product and variant, price it per channel, publish it, and background tasks make it searchable with correct prices.

steps.text: The dashboard sends GraphQL mutations to the single API endpoint; each is resolved by a mutation class registered in ProductMutations.
productCreate validates the input, saves the Product with search_index_dirty set and fires product_created. The product exists but is not in any channel yet.
Attribute input is validated per input type and saved: missing AttributeValue rows are bulk-created and linked to the product.
productVariantCreate adds a variant with SKU (stock keeping unit), stocks and attributes, makes it the default variant if it is the first, and marks promotion rules in the product's channels dirty.
productChannelListingUpdate upserts a ProductChannelListing per channel with is_published, publication date, visible in listings and available for purchase, and can add the variant to the channel.
productVariantChannelListingUpdate sets the variant price in the channel currency and copies it into discounted_price until the background recalculation runs.
Both listing mutations mark the product listing in the touched channels with discounted_price_dirty.
Within the beat interval (30 seconds by default) the task recalculates the discounted price, applying any matching promotion, and clears the dirty flag.
The search beat task picks up products with search_index_dirty and rebuilds their weighted search vector.
A shopper's products query in that channel now includes the product, because it is published and has a sellable variant listing with a price.

flows.name: A promotion changes the prices shoppers see
flows.summary: A catalogue promotion is created, its rules are matched to variants in the background, and stored discounted prices update.

steps.text: promotionCreate bulk-creates the rules. Catalogue rules with a reward, predicate and channels are flagged variants_dirty; nothing is priced yet.
This check decides which rules qualify: only catalogue promotions with a positive reward, a value type, a non-empty predicate and at least one channel.
The beat task takes up to 50 dirty rules of active promotions and records their current variants.
Each rule's catalogue predicate (products, variants, categories, collections with AND and OR) is turned into a variant query set on the replica.
The rule-to-variant table is diffed and rewritten under row locks taken in primary key order to avoid deadlocks.
Products of both old and new variants are marked discounted_price_dirty in the rule's channels, and the rule's flag is cleared.
The second beat task recalculates dirty listings: for each variant it takes the best applicable rule, clamps at zero, and stores the cheapest variant price on the product listing.
Rules do not stack in this path: among rules valid in the channel, the one giving the largest discount wins, and the winning rule is recorded on the variant listing.
Every changed variant price triggers PRODUCT_VARIANT_DISCOUNTED_PRICE_UPDATED through the plugin manager, for apps that mirror prices.
Storefront pricing now reads the stored discounted price, shows the undiscounted range and marks the product on sale; checkout lines get the promotion through fetch_variant_rules_info.
When the start or end date passes, the toggle task sends started or ended webhooks and marks the rules dirty again, so prices follow the schedule.

flows.name: Products are exported to a file in object storage
flows.summary: Staff request a product export; a Celery task writes the file in batches to storage and notifies with a download link.

steps.text: exportProducts validates the scope (all, ids or filter) and the chosen fields, creates an ExportFile job, logs an export started event and queues the task.
The worker reads the ExportFile from the writer database (it may not be replicated yet) and runs the export.

Products are selected with the same ProductFilter the API uses, headers are built from the requested fields, attributes, warehouses and channels, and a temporary CSV (comma-separated values) or Excel file is created.
Products are read from the replica in batches of 1,000 with prefetches, flattened into rows and appended to the file.
The finished file is saved through Django's default storage under export_files.
Plugins are notified of success with an absolute download link, and product_export_completed fires; ExportTask marks the job successful.
Every night at 01:00 files older than EXPORT_FILES_TIMEDELTA (30 days by default) are deleted from storage with their rows.
